title: October 2026 PPI Up 6.5 Percent: Build the 2027 Cost Inflation Table From the Books by Vendor and Account, Test Your Pass-Through, and Set Prices Before the Fed's December Hike
excerpt: The October 2026 PPI shows producer prices up 6.5 percent over twelve months, with goods up 10.2 percent, freight up 18.5 percent, and energy up 37 percent, while the CPI has no annual rate at all. Here is how a finance team builds its 2027 cost inflation table from its own ledgers by vendor and account, measures how much of 2026's cost increase it actually passed through, phases the FIFO lag, and sets the price and interest assumptions before the Fed's December 8 to 9 meeting.
author: FinBoard Team
coverAlt: Finance team mapping the October 2026 PPI category table onto a multi-entity cost of goods sold ledger by vendor and account for the 2027 budget
content:
The October 2026 PPI puts producer prices up 6.5 percent over twelve months, the largest rise since 2022, while the CPI has no annual rate. Don't budget 2027 with one inflation number. Build a cost inflation table from the books by vendor and account, measure last year's pass-through, and set 2027 prices from it.

Why this matters now

The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the October 2026 Producer Price Index on 2026-11-13. Final demand prices rose 0.3 percent in the month and 6.5 percent for the twelve months ended in October, which the release calls the largest 12-month rise since moving up 7.4 percent in November 2022. Underneath the headline, final demand goods rose 10.2 percent, energy 37.0 percent, and transportation and warehousing services 18.5 percent, while services other than trade and transportation rose 3.2 percent. Further up the supply chain, processed goods for intermediate demand rose 14.6 percent and unprocessed goods 16.9 percent. Those are your suppliers' suppliers, and their increases have not finished arriving on your invoices.

Three days earlier, on 2026-11-10, the same agency released the October 2026 Consumer Price Index with a 0.4 percent monthly increase and no 12-month change at all, because October 2025 prices were never collected during the lapse in appropriations. So the index that measures what your customers pay has no annual rate this month, and the index that measures what you pay has its highest annual rate in four years. A finance team that budgets 2027 with a single inflation assumption copied from a headline is choosing between a number that does not exist and a number that does not describe its cost lines.

The rate side moved the same week. In a speech in London on 2026-11-10, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he was leaning toward supporting a 25 basis point increase at the December meeting, that he was particularly concerned about the breadth of price increases, and that if the data came in worse a 50 basis point hike should be considered because hiking only 25 basis points would put the Fed's credibility at risk. CFO Dive reported on 2026-11-10 that futures traders moved the odds of a hike at the December 8 to 9 meeting to 100 percent, with 11.8 percent odds of a half point. The interest line in the 2027 budget is moving at the same time as the cost lines.

Coverage of the release explains the economy. PYMNTS on 2026-11-13 walked through the monthly path and quoted an economist on transportation as the channel that carries energy costs into core goods. Budgeting guides such as Capstone CFO's 2027 budget article of 2026-10-15 say to build costs from vendor contracts and unit costs and to treat pricing as the biggest lever. Both are right as far as they go. Neither shows a controller how to turn a PPI table and three QuickBooks files into a per-account inflation assumption, how to measure what share of 2026's cost increase the company actually recovered in price, or when a supplier increase reaches cost of goods sold through FIFO inventory. That is this article.

What the October 2026 PPI says about each of your cost lines

The PPI is published by commodity and by stage of production, not by chart of accounts. The useful step is to map each cost account, and where possible each vendor, to the index line that prices what the vendor sells you. The table uses the 12-month unadjusted changes and the seasonally adjusted September to October changes from Table 2 of the release.

Two things in the table matter for the budget. The first is dispersion. The foods index rose 1.7 percent, but inside it fresh and dry vegetables rose 36.0 percent and eggs fell 63.5 percent. A category average is the wrong assumption for any account where one or two vendors dominate. The second is the gap between what producers pay and what they charge. Inputs to construction rose 12.4 percent while the price of final demand construction rose 5.5 percent. That 6.9 point gap is contractors absorbing cost, and the same test applies to you: compare the inflation in your purchases to the inflation in your own selling prices.

Timing matters as much as level. A Federal Reserve Bank of New York analysis published 2026-10-06 found that after a cost shock, domestic producer prices rise only a little in the first six months and then roughly double over the following six, and that a 10 percent increase in import and producer prices raised retail prices by about 5.6 percent. Read that from the buyer's side: increases already in the October PPI will keep arriving in vendor invoices through mid 2027, and the companies you sell to will push back on recovering more than about half of them.

One company, three ledgers, one cost inflation table: the walk-through

Call it Kestrel Packaging Group: a film plant, a corrugated plant, and a distribution entity, each in its own QuickBooks Online file, about $62 million of 2026 revenue, FIFO perpetual inventory, and a $12 million floating rate term loan. The numbers are illustrative. The sequence is not.

Step one: pull 2026 spend by account and vendor across all three entities

The controller exports every purchase transaction for the trailing twelve months from the three files and groups it by cost of goods sold account, then by vendor, then by month. Cost of goods sold is $40.0 million: resin and film materials $22.0 million, freight in and out $4.0 million, plant energy $2.0 million, direct labor $9.0 million, and packaging supplies and maintenance $3.0 million. Gross profit is $22.0 million, 35.5 percent of revenue. Eighty percent of the materials line sits with four vendors, which is where the vendor-level work pays off. A vendor spend analysis built the same way is the starting file.

Step two: split each line into price and volume from the invoices

For every vendor with unit pricing on its invoices, the controller computes the average invoice price per unit for 2026 against 2025 at constant mix. Resin and film averaged 11 percent higher, below the 17.1 percent industrial chemicals index because two supply contracts reprice quarterly with a lag. Freight rates per shipment rose 14 percent. Energy rates per kilowatt hour and per therm rose 30 percent. Direct labor rates rose 4 percent after the April review. Supplies rose about 5 percent, in line with the goods less foods and energy index, which is the assumption used where no unit data exists.

The price-only portion of the 2026 cost increase is the current spend less what the same volume would have cost at 2025 prices: $2.18 million on materials, $0.49 million on freight, $0.46 million on energy, $0.35 million on labor, and $0.14 million on supplies, about $3.62 million in total. That is the number the budget never showed, because the budget was built with 3 percent on everything.

Step three: measure what was actually passed through

The same exercise on the revenue side, average selling price per unit at constant mix, shows prices up 3.5 percent in 2026, worth about $2.10 million on $62 million of revenue. The pass-through ratio is $2.10 million of price recovered against $3.62 million of price-driven cost, or 58 percent. The $1.52 million not recovered is 2.5 points of gross margin, and it is the whole explanation for the margin slide that the monthly budget versus actual review attributed to mix. Mix was never the problem. Price was.

Step four: set 2027 assumptions per line, with the source written down

Each line gets its own assumption and its own evidence. Materials: supplier letters announce a 9 percent reset on January 1 covering 60 percent of volume, and the remaining contracts hold until July, so the blended 2027 assumption is 8 percent, documented against the 17.1 percent index and the letters. Freight: 10 percent, from the carriers' published 2027 general rate increases, checked against the 18.5 percent index. Energy: 12 percent, from the utility's filed rate case rather than the 37.0 percent index, which is dominated by fuels Kestrel does not buy. Labor: 4 percent from the compensation plan. Supplies: 3 percent. The 2027 cost increase at flat volume is $1.76 million plus $0.40 million plus $0.24 million plus $0.36 million plus $0.09 million, $2.85 million in total. A single 3 percent assumption would have budgeted $1.20 million and understated cost by $1.65 million.

Step five: phase the FIFO lag by month

Materials inventory on the balance sheet is $5.5 million, about three months of purchases. Under FIFO the January 1 price increase enters inventory on January invoices (debit inventory, credit accounts payable at the new price) and reaches cost of goods sold only as those units are sold, so the full 9 percent appears in cost of goods sold from April. The budget phases materials inflation at the old price in the first quarter and the new price from the second. A company on standard cost sees it sooner: the excess of invoice price over standard is debited to purchase price variance in the month of purchase, credited to accounts payable, and the variance is a flow item that lands in the income statement before the unit sells. Either way, the point-in-time inventory balance carries the increase before the flow measure shows it, and a reviewer should be able to tie the two.

Step six: decide the price action and the interest line

To hold gross margin at 35.5 percent on $42.85 million of cost, Kestrel needs revenue of $66.4 million, a 7.1 percent average price increase at flat volume. To hold gross profit dollars at $22.0 million it needs 4.6 percent. The CFO takes both numbers to the sales leadership with the per-customer contract reset dates, because a 7.1 percent increase on everyone is not a decision, it is an average. On the interest line, a 25 basis point move on the $12 million floating rate loan is $30,000 a year and a 50 basis point move is $60,000, small next to the cost table but dated, so the model carries the December 9 decision date the same way the cash forecast rebuilt after the September hike carried the reset.

Step seven: the table itself

The deliverable is one table per entity and one consolidated: cost account, top vendors, 2026 spend, 2026 price variance from the books, the mapped PPI line and its 12-month change, the 2027 assumption, the evidence for it, the month it takes effect, the FIFO lag, and the owner. It replaces one cell in the budget model with a page the board can question line by line. A company that ran its CPI escalation clauses through the same discipline last week already has the contract register the table needs.

Accounting controls for a 2027 cost inflation budget

Source data: the purchase transactions by account, vendor, and month from each entity's ledger for 2025 and 2026; vendor invoices with unit prices and quantities for the top vendors; sales invoices with units for the price per unit calculation; the inventory subledger balance and turns; supplier price letters, carrier general rate increase notices, the utility rate case, and the compensation plan; the BLS PPI release of 2026-11-13 with its Table 2 by commodity, recorded with its date; the loan agreement's rate reset terms; and the 2027 budget model's cost input cells.

Calculation: a fixed sequence anyone can rerun. Group spend by account and vendor. For each vendor with unit data, compute the 2026 average price per unit against 2025 at constant mix; the price variance is current spend less current volume at the prior price. Where unit data is missing, apply the mapped PPI line and label it as a proxy. Sum price variances by account. Compute selling price realization the same way on the revenue side and divide price recovered by price-driven cost for the pass-through ratio. Set one 2027 assumption per account with its evidence, multiply by budgeted volume, and phase by month using the inventory turn for FIFO lines. Polarity: purchases debit inventory or expense and credit accounts payable; cost of goods sold is a flow measure that moves only when inventory is relieved; purchase price variance is a flow debit in the period of purchase; inventory is a point-in-time balance that must agree to units on hand at their FIFO layers. Never net the price variance against the volume variance in one line, because the budget question is which one the company controls.

Review: a second person reties the spend by account to each entity's trial balance and to the consolidated total; recomputes the price per unit for the top vendors from invoices, not from the summary; confirms the PPI line mapped to each account describes what the vendor actually sells; checks every 2027 assumption against its written evidence and flags any that is last year's number plus a round figure; ties the FIFO phasing to the inventory turn; and confirms the pass-through ratio uses constant mix on both sides.

Decision: the controller owns the table, the price variance math, and the phasing. The CFO owns the 2027 assumptions and the pass-through target, because they set the price action the company will take to customers. Sales leadership owns the per-customer price decisions and their dates. The board owns the margin it will accept if pass-through falls short. The suppliers own their letters, and until a reset is confirmed in writing the assumption stands at the controller's documented estimate.

Limits and common mistakes

The PPI measures prices received by domestic producers. It is not your vendor's price list. Use it to test and to fill gaps, not to replace invoice data where you have it.

Twelve-month changes include a year of volatile energy. Diesel up 115.2 percent and energy up 37.0 percent over the year arrived with a monthly decline in October. A budget that extrapolates the annual rate on energy will overstate it, and one that extrapolates the monthly change will understate it. Use the rate case or the fuel contract where one exists.

Constant mix matters. A price per unit that blends products will report mix as price. Where the ledger lacks units, say so in the table and use the proxy.

Seasonally adjusted monthly figures and unadjusted 12-month figures are different series. The table shows them side by side, as the BLS release does. Do not combine them in one calculation.

Pass-through is not a target of 100 percent. The New York Fed research puts retail pass-through near half. A company that budgets full recovery without a contract that provides it is budgeting hope.

The Fed decision is not made. Odds of 100 percent are a market price, not an outcome. Carry the date and both sizes until December 9.

Kestrel is illustrative. The index values, dates, and quotations come from the BLS, Federal Reserve, CFO Dive, New York Fed, PYMNTS, and Capstone CFO sources cited above.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the October 2026 PPI report show?

The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3 percent in October 2026 and 6.5 percent over the twelve months ended in October, the largest 12-month increase since November 2022. Final demand goods rose 10.2 percent over the year, energy 37.0 percent, transportation and warehousing services 18.5 percent, and services other than trade and transportation 3.2 percent. Processed goods for intermediate demand rose 14.6 percent. BLS published the release on November 13, 2026, and the November data are scheduled for December 15, 2026.

Why shouldn't a 2027 budget use one inflation rate for all costs?

Because the October 2026 PPI shows cost inflation ranging from a 63.5 percent decline in eggs to a 115.2 percent increase in diesel fuel, with freight up 18.5 percent and industrial chemicals up 17.1 percent against a 5.2 percent rise in goods less foods and energy. One rate applied to every account will be wrong on every line, and the resulting budget versus actual variances cannot be explained. Map each cost account to the PPI line that prices what its vendors sell, then replace the proxy with invoice data wherever unit prices exist.

How do I measure my company's cost pass-through from the books?

Compute the price-only part of the cost increase: for each vendor with unit prices, current spend less current volume priced at last year's rate, summed by account. Compute price realization the same way on sales invoices, at constant product mix. Divide price recovered by price-driven cost. A ratio of 58 percent means the company absorbed 42 percent of its input inflation in gross margin. Run the calculation per entity and consolidated, because pass-through usually differs by customer base.

When does a supplier price increase reach cost of goods sold under FIFO?

When the units bought at the new price are sold, not when they are bought. The purchase is debited to inventory and credited to accounts payable at the new price, and cost of goods sold moves only as inventory is relieved. If inventory on hand equals three months of purchases, a January 1 increase reaches cost of goods sold in April. Companies on standard cost see it earlier because the excess of invoice over standard is debited to purchase price variance in the month of purchase.

How should the December Fed decision enter the 2027 budget?

As a dated assumption with two sizes. Governor Waller said on November 10, 2026 that he leaned toward a 25 basis point increase at the December 8 to 9 meeting and that a 50 basis point move should be considered if the data worsened, and futures markets priced a hike at 100 percent. Multiply each size by the floating rate balance, record the reset date from the loan agreement, and replace the assumption with the actual decision on December 9.

Once every cost line has its own assumption, its evidence, and its month, the 2027 budget stops being a single inflation cell and becomes a table the board can test.
